transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

Yes — on many Beko washer-dryers, using water during a drying-only programme is normal. They use a small flow of cold water to condense the moisture removed from the clothes, then pump that water away. So hearing water enter and drain while drying, even with fairly dry clothes, does not by itself mean there is a fault. What matters is the amount and result:
1. A small/intermittent trickle and normal drying is expected.
2. A strong continuous flow, water leaking, an unusual drain overflow, or clothes no longer drying properly would point to a problem with the condensing water path, inlet valve/control, or drainage. Check that the cold-water tap is fully on and that neither the inlet hose nor drain hose behind the machine is kinked or squashed. Do this with the machine switched off if you need to move it. Is it only a small intermittent trickle of water, and does the machine still dry the clothes normally?
Yes, it's only a gentle trickle with the pump coming on now and then, and the clothes come out properly dry. No leaks on the floor either.

That sounds normal rather than a fault. A gentle trickle of cold water with the pump running from time to time is how many Beko washer-dryers condense moisture during a drying-only cycle. As it is drying properly and there are no leaks, there is no indication of a failed part. When the machine is switched off, it is still worth checking the cold-water tap is fully open and the inlet and drain hoses behind it are not kinked or trapped. A restricted supply can affect drying performance, while a restricted drain could eventually cause water to back up. If drying becomes poor, the water flow turns into a strong continuous rush, or it starts leaking, then the condensing-water path or drainage would need investigating. On the present symptoms, carry on using it normally.

candidates: Water supply or drain arrangement issue if the flow is excessive or drying performance has changed (low)
